liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Playin' In The Band** (2 reviews): Playin' is described as far out; Playin' through Drums and Space into Truckin' is a large stretch of focused, quality jamming [27][35]
- **One More Saturday Night** (2 reviews): The opener is called killer, with energy carrying in from the previous song's end; Opener has energy but is marred by some rough changes [27][30]
- **Let It Grow** (1 review): Let It Grow stood out on first listen as having something special [24]
- **Samson And Delilah** (1 review): The Samson, Terrapin, Playin' sequence was singled out as special on first listen [24]
- **Terrapin Station** (1 review): Terrapin is nicely played in the second set, which is better than the first [30]

## Setlist highlights

- **One One More Saturday Night**: back after 110 archived shows (595 days); rare: 4 archived performances [36]
- **we'll be right back**: earliest performance in the archive; mythic rare: 2 archived performances [36]
- **delete - replaced by track 18**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [36]

## The recordings

- **gd84-12-29.oade-schoeps.ladner.24294.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): source not stated; 18 songs; 160 min; rated 3.5/5 by 4 [1]. Said about its sound: Reviewer says the sound at the Civic was good and the tape sounds great; Very clean transfer, arrived already mastered for CD dynamic range, seamless and expertly tracked [1][28]
- **gd1984-12-29.140187.fob.cmc4-mk41.oade.bryant.wise.miller.clugston.flac1644**: source not stated; 18 songs; 155 min [2]
- **gd1984-12-29.142761.sbd.miller.flac1648**: soundboard; 17 songs; 154 min; rated 4.33/5 by 3 [3]
- **gd1984-12-29.150895.fm.waddell.haines.clugston.flac2448**: FM broadcast; 17 songs; 156 min [5]
- **gd1984-12-29.senn421.mccue.ford.81758.sbeok.flac16**: source not stated; 17 songs; 153 min; rated 4.33/5 by 3 [11]. Said about its sound: A very nice audience recording with solid music; the first set is brief [30]
- **gd1984-12-29.132520.fob-schoeps.Oade.BCE.flac16**: source not stated; 16 songs; 158 min; rated 4/5 by 1 [12]. Said about its sound: An audience tape with a fair amount of echo [34]
- **gd84-12-29.aud.12926.sbefail.shnf**: audience recording; 17 songs; 151 min; rated 3.5/5 by 2 [15]. Said about its sound: For an audience recording it is very good: full, clean sound, not muddy like some others [26]
- **gd1984-12-29.nak100.holtz-bolton.jaz.105032.flac16**: source not stated; 15 songs; 149 min; rated 4/5 by 2 [23]. Said about its sound: Recording is very clear and well-rounded but needs pitch correction; Cassidy sounds about a quarter tone sharp [32]

## Around the show

- Atmosphere was subdued because Steve Parrish's wife and kids died in a car wreck after the previous night's show [28]
- Special circumstances surrounded these shows, making the playing very emotional for the band and the fans [34]
- Reviewer found the show lively and energetic by 1984 standards, perhaps thanks to the Oade taper [24]
- Reviewer considers this an overlooked show, well played but not a standout 'wow' show [26]
- The night before had Phil with a new mic, returning to regular singing, plus two breakouts [28]
- Reviewer calls it a strong show for the period, with a liquid second set [35]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd84-12-29.oade-schoeps.ladner.24294.sbeok.shnf**: taped by Doug Oade; transferred by Chris Ladner; source: Oade Recording (FOB Schoeps CMC 441> Oade M118 > Sony TC D5)>DATs > CDR > WAV > SHN [1]
- **gd1984-12-29.140187.fob.cmc4-mk41.oade.bryant.wise.miller.clugston.flac1644**: taped by Jim Wise and Robert Bryant patched out of Oade Brothers; transferred by Charlie Miller and Scott Clugston; source: 1st Set: (FOB) Schoeps CMC4/MK41 > Oade M118 > Cassette Master (Sony WM-D6C/Denon DXM-90)2nd Set: (FOB) Schoeps CMC4/MK41 > Oade M118 > Sony PCM-F1 [2]. Also: A Schoeps PCM source supplies the crowd and the first four seconds of One More Saturday Night [2]
- **gd1984-12-29.142761.sbd.miller.flac1648**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD > Cassette Master > Reel (Technics) > Dat (Panasonic SV-3800/48k) [3]. Also: Soundboard source from DATs provided by Rob Eaton, with a patch source from Joani Walker and Paul Scotton, pitch corrected [3]
- **gd1984-12-29.150895.fm.waddell.haines.clugston.flac2448**: taped by Jamie Waddell; transferred by Jay Haines; source: FM Broadcast Mix > (?PCM?) > Cassettes [5]. Also: Source cassettes from Jamie Waddell, transferred by Jay Haines; a FOB Neumann KM84i source supplies the crowd and start of Samson; Tape flips were all overlapped, leading to speculation that it derives from a PCM master [5]
- **gd1984-12-29.senn421.mccue.ford.81758.sbeok.flac16**: taped by Mark McCue; transferred by Alex Ford; source: MAC; 2 Sennheiser 421s > Sony D5 > Sony D5 > Maxell MX 90s [11]
- **gd1984-12-29.132520.fob-schoeps.Oade.BCE.flac16**: taped by Oade Brothers; transferred by Dan McDonald and Dave Usborne; source: Source: Schoeps CMC441s (90deg, 17cm) > Oade M118 > Oade mod SONY PCM-F1; [12]
- **gd84-12-29.aud.12926.sbefail.shnf**: source: AUD>?>CDR>EAC>SHN>WAV(re-tracked)>SHN [15]
- **gd1984-12-29.nak100.holtz-bolton.jaz.105032.flac16**: taped by Greg Holtz and Tony Bolton; transferred by JAZ; source: Nakamichi CM-100s w/CP-4 shotgun caps -> Sony TC-D5M. Front Row Balcony [23]

claims.text: Let It Grow stood out on first listen as having something special
The Samson, Terrapin, Playin' sequence was singled out as special on first listen
Reviewer found the show lively and energetic by 1984 standards, perhaps thanks to the Oade taper
For an audience recording it is very good: full, clean sound, not muddy like some others
Reviewer considers this an overlooked show, well played but not a standout 'wow' show
The opener is called killer, with energy carrying in from the previous song's end
Playin' is described as far out
Atmosphere was subdued because Steve Parrish's wife and kids died in a car wreck after the previous night's show
Reviewer says the sound at the Civic was good and the tape sounds great
The night before had Phil with a new mic, returning to regular singing, plus two breakouts
A very nice audience recording with solid music; the first set is brief
Opener has energy but is marred by some rough changes
Terrapin is nicely played in the second set, which is better than the first
Recording is very clear and well-rounded but needs pitch correction; Cassidy sounds about a quarter tone sharp
Special circumstances surrounded these shows, making the playing very emotional for the band and the fans
An audience tape with a fair amount of echo
Playin' through Drums and Space into Truckin' is a large stretch of focused, quality jamming
Reviewer calls it a strong show for the period, with a liquid second set
Oade recording: FOB Schoeps CMC 441 into Oade M118 and Sony TC D5, then DATs, CDR, WAV, SHN
Very clean transfer, arrived already mastered for CD dynamic range, seamless and expertly tracked
First set from Robert Bryant's master cassette, patched from the Oade brothers; second set from Jim Wise; transfers by Charlie Miller
A Schoeps PCM source supplies the crowd and the first four seconds of One More Saturday Night
Soundboard source from DATs provided by Rob Eaton, with a patch source from Joani Walker and Paul Scotton, pitch corrected
Source cassettes from Jamie Waddell, transferred by Jay Haines; a FOB Neumann KM84i source supplies the crowd and start of Samson
Tape flips were all overlapped, leading to speculation that it derives from a PCM master
